label: Dahi
comment: Soured by mesophilic lactococci at about 22 °C, so not a yoghurt (Codex does not count it as one).

about.text: Dahi is a traditional yogurt or fermented milk product originating from and popular throughout the Indian subcontinent. It is usually prepared from cows' milk, and sometimes buffalo milk or goat milk. The word curd is used in Indian English to refer to homemade yogurt, while the term yogurt refers to the pasteurized commercial variety known as "heat-treated fermented milk".

how.text: Mesophilic lactococci sour boiled milk into a soft set curd; diacetyl-forming Lc. diacetylactis and Leuconostoc give mild dahi its buttery note, while added thermophiles make a sourer dahi. Household dahi is backslopped from the previous batch, so its flora varies, with Lactobacillus and Streptococcus often dominant. The 37 °C, 5–8 h route with added thermophiles gives a sourer, yoghurt-like dahi.

facts.v: Acidity at most 0.7 % lactic acid for sweet dahi, at most 1.0 % for sour dahi

Boiled milk backslopped, 2-3 days at room temperature; Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis and subsp. cremoris, Enterococcus faecalis, E. faecium and E. durans found (the paper's tables disagree on some strain assignments)
Dahi churned 10-15 min for butter (gheu); the remaining mohi heated 15-20 min to curdle
